answer: A registry can require each agent to stake a deposit locked like quartz in a vault: one identity is cheap, but a thousand fake identities means a thousand deposits frozen. Peers rate behaviour, and an agent that misbehaves forfeits its stake while honest agents earn theirs back with interest. Like onyx forming only under pressure, reputation accrues slowly, so a Sybil attacker pays real capital per identity and waits months to look trustworthy, while a mesa of honest agents with long checkable histories simply outvotes the fakes.
